incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as fully revised), Articles 288 through 317, and in particular Article 289 (articles of

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax System (www.hometax.go.kr) for tax registration, e-invoicing and VAT filing; Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (www.unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident company operating in Korea must complete HomeTax business registration. Step 1: Confirm existence of a domestic place of business or appoint a Korean tax representative if no fixed place of business exists. Step 2: Prepare a business registration package comprising (i) proof of foreign statutory existence and registration certificate of the foreign company, (ii) notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized articles of incorporation and board resolution approving the Korean establishment or representative, (iii) power of attorney to the Korean tax representative, (iv) lease agreement or other documentary evidence of the Korean place of business, (v) identification documents of the responsible officer/director, and (vi) opening financial statement of the Korean operation. Step 3: Submit the application via HomeTax or in person to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean place of business; a foreign company without a fixed place of business registers with the Seoul District Tax Office. Step 4: The NTS verifies the filing and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the VAT ID, corporate TIN, and employer withholding registration number. Step 5: For a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa, complete Commercial Court incorporation, obtain a corporate seal registration, and file the NTS tax registration within one month of business commencement; foreign ownership is permitted and does not alter the registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not operate a check-the-box pass-through election or a domestic hybrid mismatch election for a Chusik Hoesa; the entity is mandatorily taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, with foreign branches or CFCs subject to separate Korean rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No revenue-based registration threshold: all persons carrying on business in Korea, including foreign non-resident suppliers and Chusik Hoesa corporations, must register for VAT from commencement of taxable supplies. A simplified VAT regime for individual entrepreneurs below KRW 80 million taxable turnover does not apply to corporations or foreign companies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issuance through the NTS HomeTax electronic invoice system or NTS-certified EDI/API channel. E-invoicing is compulsory for all corporate VAT registrants and for individual entrepreneurs whose prior-year taxable supplies exceed KRW 100 million. The invoice data is transmitted to NTS in near real time and matched against VAT returns; no separate fiscal clearance stamp is used, but anti-fraud validation is performed by the NTS digital invoice database, and failure to transmit can carry additional tax penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported from Korea upon export declaration acceptance, to supplies related to international maritime or aviation services, and to services performed for or used outside Korea where the recipient is a foreign non-resident. For a virtual card issuer, cross-border card issuing, transaction processing, interchange and settlement fees will qualify as zero-rated exported services only where the substantive service is performed outside Korea for a non-resident customer; the company must prove the overseas use or delivery, the identity and location of the customer, and the actual receipt of currency from a foreign source. Domestic B2B or consumer card transactions in Korea remain subject to the 10% VAT rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration record accepted through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Customs export clearance confirmation or export approval number
Commercial invoice and VAT tax invoice evidencing zero-rated supply
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for goods; for services, signed service contract and overseas delivery/performance evidence
Packing list and freight forwarding documentation
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or foreign currency remittance advice issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict NTS audit review. If documentation does not substantiate the export or the foreign use of the service, the NTS will assess VAT at 10% on the full supply value, impose additional taxes for under-declared VAT and unfaithful tax invoices (commonly 10% to 40% of the underpaid amount depending on negligence, intent or evasion), levy statutory late-payment interest, and may prosecutionally pursue fraudulent export invoice cases. The statutory assessment window is extended to 10 years where the zero-rating claim is supported by false documents; previously claimed input VAT refunds are recoverable with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with policy and supervisory coordination by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but fully regulated convertibility framework. Current-account payments for trade, services, and profit remittance are generally unrestricted and may be processed through domestic banks; however, every external payment requires a valid foreign exchange purpose classification and, where transactional thresholds are exceeded, prior or post reporting to the Bank of Korea through the reporting bank or Korea Customs Service. Capital-account operations are subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification, FDI registration, and supporting evidence requirements. The Korean won is not freely accessible offshore in a fully unrestricted manner because the KRW is not deliverable outside Korea in significant volume; cross-border KRW settlement is generally restricted to legitimate trade and investment flows. For a corporate virtual card issuer, routine settlement with card network processors is permissible, but proceeds in foreign currency must pass through a domestic foreign-currency account, and profit remittances require a clear sponsor/license and tax clearance document. The automated teller machine style conversion is not available for high-risk fintech treasury operations; every treasury transaction must be tested against the underlying commercial identity, card network settlement schedules, and ISIC/ELF compliance declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect export proceeds within six months of the export declaration/customs clearance date; the period may be extended by the head of Korea Customs Service or the Minister of Economy and Finance for justified causes. There is no compulsory foreign-exchange surrender ratio for ordinary export receipts under the current free-floating regime, so the mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; exporters may credit the proceeds to a licensed domestic foreign-currency account and convert at commercial rates as needed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Won Account and Corporate Foreign-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Direct Investment Deposit Account and Basic Operational Account
Trade Settlement Account and Virtual Card Settlement Clearing Account
Operational Current Account and Foreign Exchange Hedge Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Offshore digital-only EMI providers are not recognized as authorized banks for the purpose of holding a resident Korean corporation's treasury balances. South Korea requires foreign-exchange business and payment services to be conducted through a locally licensed institution under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. A Korean Chusik Hoesa must open its primary operating and settlement accounts at a domestic commercial bank or registered brokerage/securities firm; an offshore EMI may at most provide a technical card management or program management interface if a domestically licensed credit-card issuing company underwrites the card scheme. It cannot legally service the entity's corporate deposits or provide cross-border clearing rails independently.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch identity verification is the statutory baseline under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. For a high-risk virtual card issuer, the statutory representative and, when personally controlling 25 percent or more of shares, the beneficial owner must appear at a domestic commercial bank branch with passport, Alien Registration Card if applicable, corporate seal certificate subject to notarization, articles of incorporation, and an officer resignation/retention registry. Remote consular proxy opening is not a recognized standard for this risk tier; even a notarized power of attorney will generally trigger an additional video or face-to-face compliance interview with the bank's International AML Committee due to the entity's fintech and cross-border card issuing profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or deviation between statutory officers on the corporate registry and actual controlling persons, potentially masked by nominee directors or multi-layer overseas shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the complete corporate registry extract (Gibu), a certified share register, a legal entity structure chart, passport copies and ID documents for every individual owning or controlling in aggregate 25 percent or more of shares or voting rights, signed director appointments, and a notarized statement of no nominee arrangement; also provide a six-month capitalization and shareholder funding audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory classification mismatch: the virtual expense card issuing business may look like unregulated card arbitrage rather than a licensed financial service, exposing the bank to money service business liability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the FSS license or registration certificate issued under the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act and/or Electronic Financial Transactions Act, the program manager agreement with the issuing bank or Mastercard/Visa BIN sponsor, the ISIC 6619 classification rationale, and evidence that the entity has obtained all Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) certifications and anti-money laundering program manuals and independent AML audit reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire profile inconsistent with declared fintech operation: high frequency of mixed-purpose transfers, round-dollar treasury movements, or rapid pass-through of funds to third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the underlying customer agreements, merchant settlement schedules, sample expense card transaction log, signed invoices or purchase orders for treasury disbursements, projected cash-flow model, and the official FX transaction declaration forms previously filed at the bank; a certification that all SWIFT wires bear correct intended FX purpose codes and that no transaction breaches the 10,000 USD reporting threshold is also required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and virtual asset exposure links through corporate card loads or settlement corridors in jurisdictions with AML/CFT deficiencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening report covering all cardholders and corporate clients, a banned-jurisdiction list embedded in the card programme, an annual independent sanctions compliance audit, and evidence that virtual asset deposits or crypto-funded loads are contractually prohibited and operationally blocked by the card issuer platform.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: In-bound foreign equity contributions must be lodged as Foreign Direct Investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before the remittance. The investor submits a declaration to a domestic bank or KOTRA, obtains an FDI registration certificate, and then sends the funds via SWIFT MT103 in the investor's name using the FX purpose code corresponding to inward direct investment. The receiving bank credits the corporate foreign-currency escrow/deposit account and later converts to KRW with the precise FDI declaration. Capital verification is performed by the bank against the FDI registration certificate, the MT103 SWIFT message, the investor's capital account record, and the paid-in capital ledger of the Chusik Hoesa. Dividends or return-of-capital outbound remittances must be supported by audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, and an FX remittance application showing the earnings were legally generated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury payments use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border purchase, commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for documentary trade settlements, and documentary collections where the card-funded supplier requires shipping-document confirmation. Virtual card transactions flow independently through Mastercard/Visa network settlement to merchant acquirer banks; the licensed card issuer must maintain a settlement bank account in Korea and settle net card balances in KRW to the merchant acquirer through the network, with foreign-currency exposure offset by domestic bank FX contracts. All outbound wires must include the correct Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code and maintain source-of-funds documentation for every beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won foreign exchange forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank supported by a genuine underlying trade or card settlement exposure (real demand principle under Foreign Exchange Transactions Act)

Deliverable cross-currency swaps with a licensed domestic bank for hedging contracted foreign-currency cash flows, provided the swap is booked under the entity's treasury policy and reported to the Bank of Korea where required

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as a primary onshore hedge; NDFs may be considered only outside the regulated Korean banking system to hedge third-party investor exposure and must never interfere with domestic bank settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March, with an automatic one-month extension available when the return is prepared and transmitted by a certified tax accountant under the NTS e-filing extension procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported income attracts a 20% penalty tax and under-reported income attracts a 10% penalty tax; overdue corporate tax accrues daily overdue interest at 0.022% until payment is completed. Persistent non-payment results in NTS seizure, compulsory collection, and disqualification of the delinquent director. There is no automatic administrative strike-off in Korea, but continued inactivity for five years can lead to judicial dissolution under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax return and payment of the 10% corporate-income-tax surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial, city, or municipal tax office of the registered head-office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same filing window as the national corporate tax return: for calendar-year companies, by 31 March, with extension following any corporate-tax return extension granted by the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 20% additional local-income-tax penalty for non-reporting, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% on the unpaid amount. Repeated local-tax non-compliance is treated by the Financial Services Commission as a governance and fitness failure that can support suspension or revocation of the virtual-card issuing license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report on the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the auditor's report is also delivered to the shareholders at the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor's report must be completed and delivered before the ordinary shareholders' meeting; for calendar-year companies the audited financial statements and audit report must be finalized within the three-month ordinary meeting window, i.e., by 31 March unless an extension is lawfully obtained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a mandatory external audit voids the accounts for corporate tax settlement and exposes the company and its directors to FSC sanctions, administrative fines, and disqualification orders. For a licensed virtual-card issuer, absence of a compliant external audit is a serious regulatory violation that can trigger license suspension, revocation, and director-level enforcement action by the FSS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders and formal approval of annual accounts and minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Court corporate register file; minutes are retained in the company's statutory minute book and are not annually registered unless a resolution requires registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than three months after the end of the fiscal year under Article 365 of the Korean Commercial Act; for a 31 December fiscal year, the ordinary general meeting must be held no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defaulting directors are exposed to administrative fines not exceeding KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,850) for failure to convene the ordinary meeting. The court may order the meeting to be convened, and prolonged failure to operate and hold shareholders' meetings can be a ground for judicial dissolution under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business report and regulatory return of the electronic financial business operator / virtual-card issuing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) electronic reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year, generally no later than 31 March for calendar-year operators, unless the FSS grants an explicit extension for the e-financial reporting calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit a truthful annual business report can result in an administrative penalty surcharge, suspension of business operations, an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million, and revocation of the electronic financial business license; false or reckless statements may also be subject to criminal punishment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML, KYC, and beneficial-ownership confirmation report filed with the financial intelligence unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), a dedicated unit housed at the Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing event-driven reporting throughout the year; customer records must be updated within 30 days of any beneficial-ownership change or material shareholding transfer, and the annual AML compliance program review must be completed by the internally approved date fixed in the company's AML internal calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or deficient customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership reporting can attract administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 23,000), criminal sanctions for willful violation, and license revocation under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company annual status report and 30-day reporting of foreign-investor shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance, Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), and the Financial Services Commission under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any acquisition, transfer, or conversion of foreign-invested shares must be reported within 30 days of the transaction; the consolidated annual foreign-investment status report is due by the date designated by the competent authority, generally no later than 15 April of the year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file timely foreign-investment reports exposes the foreign investor or the local entity to corrective orders, fines of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,700), and FSC remedial measures that may include restrictions on dividend outflows and license review action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is compulsory if total assets at the end of the business year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). A licensed virtual-card issuer and electronic financial business operator under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act is always subject to independent statutory audit regardless of asset size. No separate headcount threshold applies in Korea; however, the Financial Services Commission can designate an otherwise exempt company for audit based on financial dependency, shareholder dispersion, or other regulatory grounds. Listed companies are always subject to statutory audit. Because the target entity is a high-risk special-license fintech, mandatory certified CPA audit and FSS supervision apply at all times, even if its balance sheet is below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to financial services companies and FSC-supervised entities; non-designated companies may use Korean GAAP (K-GAAP), including the SME Accounting Standards for small and medium-sized enterprises. For this licensed virtual-card issuer, the Financial Supervisory Service expects accounting policies consistent with K-IFRS or the K-GAAP framework, read together with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the External Audit and Accounting Standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO form filed with a companies registry for every Korean stock company; instead, the financial real-name control framework under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality requires the card issuer to identify and maintain accurate records of every beneficial owner and controlling shareholder, conduct an annual risk-based refresh of all beneficial-ownership data, and update its customer file within 30 days after any share transfer, ownership change, or control event. If the entity is foreign-invested, any change in foreign-investor shareholding must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Financial Services Commission within 30 days of the transaction. Failure to refresh UBO records is treated as an AML system deficiency and may lead to administrative sanctions or license revocation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders' ledger showing classes, number, nominal value, and registered holdings of all issued shares)
Register of Directors and statutory officers (board composition, officer term expiries, appointments, and resignations)
Register of Charges or encumbrances affecting shares or assets of the company
Minute Book containing signed minutes of every ordinary and extraordinary general meeting of shareholders
Board of Directors' Minutes Book containing annual resolutions, including approval of financial statements and corporate governance matters
Share transfer and beneficial-ownership log maintained in accordance with AML and KYC procedures
External audit report archive and annual financial statements for each business year

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per annum for the company's registered office and local corporate secretarial agent in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 28,000 per annum for a regulated fintech and virtual-card issuing special-license company requiring a mandatory independent CPA audit under the K-IFRS framework

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national headline CIT, levied on progressive brackets of 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; an additional 10% local income tax surcharge yields an aggregate top rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises may access tax holidays and reductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act, including 100% national income tax exemption for a defined qualifying period and 50% reduction for a subsequent period in free economic zones; R&D expenditures on qualifying software and payment technologies are eligible for up to 25% R&D tax credits depending on entity size; technology-introduced patent and software royalty income may qualify for an IP income tax exemption or reduced tax rate; foreign tax credits are available for foreign-source income to prevent double taxation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean National Tax Service Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Corporate Tax Return) filed electronically through the HomeTax e-Service portal at www.hometax.go.kr, accompanied by the OECD-compliant local file, master file and international transaction information report schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, normally March 31 for a December 31 year-end; if the entity is subject to an external audit or has an overseas parent with a non-calendar fiscal year, the Korean filing is still due within 3 months of the Korean statutory fiscal year-end; the taxpayer may apply for an extension only upon showing unavoidable cause under the Corporate Tax Act, and late filing attracts daily penalty tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and fiscal year cost center: registered corporate name, Korean business registration number, headquarters address, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, domestic place of business, representative director name, entity classification as a Chusik Hoesa, and designated foreign investment enterprise status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Acknowledge direct and indirect non-resident ownership percentages on the shareholder tab; if foreign shareholders hold more than 50%, complete the foreign investment enterprise declaration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; failure to identify non-resident ownership triggers the domestic withholding agent obligations of the Korean corporation under the Corporate Tax Act

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement reconciliation: total gross revenue, non-taxable revenue, total expenses, disallowed expenses, provisions, depreciation and amortization adjustments, and book-to-tax adjustment schedule for the virtual card and spend management operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Included in gross income are interchange fees, merchant card network rebates, cardholder membership fees, program management fees, and interest income on cardholder float balances; deduct network scheme fees, processing costs, partnership commissions, and technical service fees only when supported by tax invoices and remittance evidence; foreign-related party service fees such as headquarters technology or shared services must be tested for arm's length deductibility

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation and net operating loss utilisation: calculation of taxable income after non-taxable income, disallowances, reserves, and carryforward loss deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim branch financing or royalties paid to the Korean Chusik Hoesa only if the corresponding income is included in the Korean taxable base; the carryforward loss deduction is capped at 80% of current-year taxable income for non-SMEs and can be used for up to 10 years; foreign-related party losses attributable to a disregarded foreign enterprise are disregarded unless arm's length substance is proven

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate corporate income tax calculation: national corporate income tax at progressive rates and the 10% local income tax surcharge computed on the national tax amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity receives foreign-source dividend or interest income already subject to a reduced treaty withholding rate, do not recalculate a domestic credit unsupported by a foreign tax certificate; where a non-resident shareholder is repatriating profits, the entity is not entitled to deduct the dividend distribution, and the domestic WHT must be recorded as an accrued liability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions: R&D credits, foreign tax credits, foreign investment tax reductions, hiring credits and prior-year overpayments, and other special tax relief under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit relief requires material evidence of foreign assessment and payment and is limited to the Korean tax attributable to foreign-source income; unused foreign tax credits carry forward for 5 years; for a virtual card issuer with overseas payment rails, document that withholding taxes paid to foreign revenue authorities are legally creditable and not claimed twice

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International transaction disclosure schedule: all transactions with foreign related parties, including intercompany royalties, technology service fees, data processing fees, loan interest, card network referral fees, cost sharing arrangements, and inventory or treasury transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is mandatory for any Korean Chusik Hoesa with related-party foreign transactions exceeding KRW 100 million in the tax year; if annual foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion, attach the approved Local File and Master File; for each transaction disclose the tested party, transfer pricing method, comparability analysis, and arm's length range, with special attention to remote SaaS fees and interchange rebate allocation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding, tax treaty and beneficial ownership declaration: outbound dividends, interest, royalties, rents, and other income paid to non-residents, including the statutory withholding tax rate and any reduced treaty rate applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a payment was made at a reduced DTA rate, the Korean payer must hold the original Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, and completed Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty; an intermediary or conduit that merely routes the payment has no treaty entitlement; any dividend from the Korean company to a foreign shareholder is a non-deductible distribution that must be reported, and WHT must be remitted to the Korean tax office by the 10th day of the following month

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Settlement statement: total tax payable, provisional tax payments, employer withholding prepayments, withheld taxes on non-resident payments, advance payments for electronic financial service fees, and final tax due or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile card customer security deposits and unused spend balances against interest income declarations; interest earned on customer float is subject to Korean corporate income tax; any foreign tax credit applied in Box 5 must be traced to the exact cash remittance statement; net tax due after credits must be paid on or before the filing deadline, and any shortfall carries daily late-payment surcharges

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate tax return attracts an unfaithful tax return penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax if the return is submitted after the deadline; underreported tax owing to negligence is penalised at 10% of the underreported amount, intentional underreporting at 40% of the underreported amount, and fraud with false inflations at 40%; unpaid or underpaid corporate tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.022% per day until fully paid; failure to submit international transaction disclosures attracts administrative penalties under the International Tax Coordination Act, and fraudulent filing by a director is a criminal offense under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine of up to 2 times the tax evaded

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate, comprising 20% national corporate withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, unless reduced or exempted by an applicable double tax treaty; for example, under the Korea-US tax treaty a 10% dividend rate may apply to a corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting stock, bringing the aggregate local-incidence treatment to 11% (10% national plus 1% local surtax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief in Korea, the foreign shareholder must provide the Korean payer with a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the relevant foreign competent authority confirming tax residence for the calendar year of payment; the foreign beneficial owner must complete and execute a Korean Beneficial Ownership Statement and an Entity Structure Statement disclosing the direct and indirect shareholders; the Korean payer must file the Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty with the competent Korean tax office, normally before the payment is made; if the statutory 22% withholding is applied, the non-resident may file a corrected claim and apply to the National Tax Service for a refund within the statutory refund prescription period, which is generally 5 years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax was paid; the Korean remitting bank will require an outward remittance justification and exchange transaction report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act before dividends can be repatriated
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for use of intangibles such as software, intellectual property, and payment technology are subject to a 22% statutory withholding rate (20% national plus 2% local income tax), with DTA reductions, for example, under the Korea-US treaty to 15% national plus 1.5% local surtax in typical industrial royalty cases; interest on intercompany loans is subject to 22% statutory withholding, but under the Korea-US treaty a general 10% national rate plus 1% local surtax may apply, and interest on loans guaranteed or insured by certain governmental export credit institutions may be exempt; intercompany royalties and interest must also satisfy the arm's length standard and transfer pricing documentation requirements, or the Korean tax authority may recharacterise excess payments as constructive dividends

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion per business year for mandatory Local File preparation and KRW 1 trillion group consolidated revenue for the Master File, while all foreign related-party transactions exceeding KRW 100 million must be reported in the annual International Transactions Report attached to the corporate tax return
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a Kuwaiti or UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation as a separate statute; instead, the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 imposes a substance-over-form principle, and the International Tax Coordination Act incorporates OECD transfer pricing substance and beneficial ownership requirements; for treaty relief, the Korean tax authority applies the beneficial ownership test and the OECD Core Income-Generating Activities analysis to determine whether the foreign recipient actually exercises decision-making functions, assumes risks, and performs substantive business activities through employees and premises; a Korean Chusik Hoesa that issues virtual cards through a foreign shell with no local management, no risk distribution, and no operating substance will be denied treaty benefits, and the CFC rules in the International Tax Coordination Act may attribute undistributed foreign income of such a shell back to Korean shareholders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Unfounded Expense Claiming
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors cause the virtual card system to issue counterfeit corporate cards for personal or fictitious entertainment, record fake card transactions, inflate interchange expenses, and understate the Korean corporate tax base; false tax invoices are created for marketing or technology services that were never rendered
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9 punishes corporate tax evasion with imprisonment not exceeding 2 years, a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax, or both; in addition, the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty, plus daily late-payment surcharges of 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount, and the National Tax Service will re-assess the Chusik Hoesa for the full deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Commercial Act Article 401, directors are jointly and severally liable to the company for damages caused by willful misconduct or gross negligence; for tax evasion, the director can be named individually in a criminal complaint, subjected to a departure restriction order, have personal bank accounts and assets attached, and be sentenced to imprisonment up to 2 years; if the company is dissolved without paying corporate tax, the court may pierce the corporate veil under the Court precedents on corporate personality abuse and hold the director personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Shell Structure Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity files a corporate tax return without the required International Transactions Report, Local File or Master File despite foreign related-party transactions exceeding the KRW 10 billion threshold; intercompany royalty or management fees are paid to a zero-substance Hong Kong or Singapore shell with no employees, no premises, and no decision-making authority, creating a taxable dividend and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Tax Coordination Act empowers the National Tax Service to disregard the intercompany arrangement, recalculate income at the arm's length price, impose additional tax on the resulting understatement, and refuse treaty relief for failure to prove beneficial ownership; under-reporting due to intentional avoidance attracts a 40% penalty and a possible criminal fine of twice the evaded tax; the law also imposes administrative fines for failure to produce mandated transfer pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who certified the tax return may be held personally liable under Commercial Act Article 401 for the company's extra tax if the abuse arose from the director's intentional act; a travel ban may be issued for the director while a tax collection investigation is open; if the shell arrangement is found to be a tax evasion device, the director may be referred to the prosecution for the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with imprisonment up to 2 years and personal restitution of the evaded tax and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Fintech Card Issuing, AML and Beneficial Ownership Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa issues physical or virtual corporate payment cards on Mastercard or Visa rails under the brand name of the entity without a license under the Credit Finance Business Act or without complying with the Electronic Financial Transactions Act registration requirements; the entity also fails to verify the ultimate beneficial owner of high-risk corporate clients, fails to file Suspicious Transaction Reports, and processes cross-border card settlement transactions for sanctioned people or shell companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed credit card issuing is administratively prohibited and may be punished under the Credit Finance Business Act with imprisonment up to 7 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million; failure to register as an electronic financial business under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act can result in a fine and cancellation of the payment network partnership; the Financial Information Act violations carry fines, and the Financial Services Commission can block the entity from the payment system; the National Tax Service will simultaneously treat the unreported fee income as hidden earnings and assess corporate tax with a 40% fraud penalty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: License violations are treated as personal criminal acts of the representative director if the director directly organized the unlicensed issuing; aside from a prison sentence, the director is jointly and severally liable to pay unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and regulatory restitution; the director is subject to an exit ban under tax collection law and can be named in sanctions enforcement lists; a court may pierce the corporate veil if the entity is used as a mere instrument for illegal card issuance and money laundering, and the director's personal assets may be attached for civil damages suffered by merchants and cardholders
